data.title: Starlink Is Years Away From Competing With AT&T and Verizon, Citi Says — But It Might Move Faster — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Al Root

Americans might have a fourth national telecom provider to complain about. SpaceX is coming, but how soon could it launch mobile service?

Citi analyst Michael Rollins sees it happening no earlier than 2029 and more likely 2030 to 2032.

That might be too conservative, but there are a few reasons for Rollins' timeline. For starters, SpaceX likely needs more wireless spectrum — essentially the pipes that carry wireless data. It has amassed about 80 megahertz of spectrum. T-Mobile US has about 400 megahertz.

SpaceX is likely to build its own ground-based network infrastructure, added Rollins in a Friday report.

The hardware alone would cost $20 billion. SpaceX would need to spend another $20 billion on more wireless spectrum. That's in addition to the ongoing spending on SpaceX's existing connectivity business. All told, additional spending on wireless communications could easily top $100 billion by 2031, he says.

It all takes time, but SpaceX could shortcut the process by just buying an existing player, Rollins says. It would also be a more capital-efficient way to launch service. Wireless telecoms trade at a discount to their assets.

For AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile, the timing matters: A faster launch would give them less time to prepare for a new national competitor.

Musk's other ventures offer an example of how quickly his companies can move. What was then xAI brought its Colossus data center in Memphis online in 122 days. But Musk's ambitious deadlines haven't always held up.

He predicted one million robo-taxis on the road by 2020 and humans on Mars by 2025. Investors are still waiting. He's also predicted 20 million Tesla vehicle sales by 2030. (Tesla is expected to sell fewer than 2 million cars in 2026.)

SpaceX stock was up 1.7% in early trading after Bloomberg reported that SpaceX wanted 80,000 cell sites.

That sent shares of cell tower companies such as Crown Castle higher on Friday. Crown and its peers are like the apartment buildings of the telecom world. Wireless companies move in with their equipment. EchoStar stock was up 2%. Its spectrum portfolio looks more valuable. (It also owns SpaceX stock.) Wireless telecom stocks, including T-Mobile, fell between 2% and 5%.

SpaceX will eventually merge its satellite communications with ground-based infrastructure to provide service. SpaceX has more than 11,000 Starlink satellites in low-Earth orbit.

Starlink is SpaceX's space-based broadband business that ended the third quarter with 13.6 million subscribers in 174 countries. Starlink's third-quarter sales and Ebitda were $5.2 billion and $3.5 billion, respectively.

Write to Al Root at allen.root@barrons.com.

data.title: GA-ASI Partnering With Spirit Defense For FQ-42 CCA Production
data.description:
SAN DIEGO, Oct 24, 2026 - (ACN Newswire) - General Atomics Aeronautical Systems, Inc. (GA-ASI), the world leader in Uncrewed Aircraft Systems (UAS), today is announcing our partnership with Spirit Defense, a Boeing Company, to support airframe production of the new FQ-42 Vengeance Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA). In June, GA-ASI won a contract from the U.S. Air Force (USAF) to produce FQ-42. Spirit Defense's role as a fuselage design-build partner brings together the company's engineering and advanced manufacturing capabilities to support the program from design through production.

GA-ASI has been the sole manufacturer of its line of UAS - which includes MQ-9A Reaper, MQ-1C Gray Eagle, MQ-20 Avenger, and MQ-9B SkyGuardian/SeaGuardian - since the company's inception in 1992. For the FQ-42 program, partnering with Spirit Defense is a strength multiplier for the company and the nation, offering manufacturing capacity and industrial depth to scale CCA production faster, while strengthening production resilience, and reducing the risk of single points of failure.

"We're excited to be working with Spirit Defense," said GA-ASI President David R. Alexander. "We've established our proven design, development, and manufacturing capability for the FQ-42. With Spirit Defense we add capacity, which is exactly the kind of production resilience our U.S. Air Force customer is looking for with its CCA ramp-up. This kind of partnership represents the scalable industrial base the Air Force and the U.S. Department of War are looking for from industry."

"We're proud to bring deep manufacturing expertise and proven capabilities to this important program," said Keith Schrader, president and CEO of Spirit Defense. "Our team understands the responsibility that comes with supporting critical national defense programs, and we're ready to deliver for our customer and the warfighter."

FQ-42 is a purpose-built, uncrewed fighter, developed with USAF as part of ongoing investment in next-generation semi-autonomous combat aircraft. The jet's modular design enables rapid integration of mission systems and mission autonomy software. GA-ASI's software architecture, demonstrated through live flight tests on multiple airframes, provides the foundation for human-machine teaming in complex combat scenarios.

Potential CCA manufacturing partnerships don't end here. Around the world, GA-ASI is in discussions with numerous international militaries interested in our Gambit Series of modular CCAs. The Gambit Series is a family of uncrewed combat jets, derived from our work on FQ-42, XQ-67A Off-Board Sensing Station, and MQ-20 Avenger, and optimized for roles such as electronic warfare, suppression of enemy air defenses (SEAD), Destruction of Enemy Air Defenses (DEAD) and stand-off precision strike, making it a versatile option for evolving security needs.

Nations interested in procuring aircraft from the Gambit Series also have an opportunity to insert indigenous manufacturing into those programs, as well as integration of their own sensors, weapons and other combat technologies.

About Spirit Defense

Spirit Defense, a Boeing Company, is an independent supplier to the defense industry. Headquartered in Wichita, Kansas, the company provides engineering, design-build, manufacturing, and lifecycle support for defense programs. Leveraging more than a century of aircraft design and manufacturing experience, Spirit Defense helps customers move innovative concepts from development to production through rapid prototyping, scalable manufacturing, and proven aerospace expertise.

About GA-ASI

General Atomics Aeronautical Systems, Inc., is the world's foremost builder of Uncrewed Aircraft Systems (UAS). Logging more than 9 million flight hours, the Predator line of UAS has flown for over 30 years and includes MQ-9A Reaper, MQ-1C Gray Eagle, MQ-20 Avenger, MQ-9B SkyGuardian/SeaGuardian, XQ-67A, and FQ-42 Vengeance. The company is dedicated to providing long-endurance, multi-mission solutions that deliver persistent situational awareness and rapid strike.

For more information, visit www.ga-asi.com.

Avenger, EagleEye, Gray Eagle, Lynx, Predator, Reaper, SeaGuardian, and SkyGuardian are trademarks of General Atomics Aeronautical Systems, Inc., registered in the United States and/or other countries.

data.title: Novartis Says MS Pill Helped Control Disease With Favorable Safety Data in Trials
data.description:
By Adria Calatayud

Novartis said its experimental multiple sclerosis pill achieved a significant reduction in symptom flare-ups in the most common form of the disease with a favorable safety profile in two late-stage studies.

The Swiss drugmaker said Friday that the studies showed its medicine--known as remibrutinib and marketed as Rhapsido for a skin condition--achieved reductions in the annualized relapse rate of 35.2% and 31.2% compared with Sanofi's Aubagio, meeting the primary goal of both trials.

This translated into one relapse every 13 years, the company said.

No liver safety signal was observed, Novartis said.

Novartis Chief Medical Officer Shreeram Aradhye said the study results point to the drug's potential to support long-term disease management by combining high efficacy with a favorable safety profile.

data.title: Berkshire Stock Is Hot Again. Is It Still a Bargain? — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Andrew Bary

The hottest megacap stock lately has been Berkshire Hathaway, which hit a record high this past week after rising almost 8% in the past month.

Berkshire is probably the ultimate defensive stock, given its diversified earnings power and fortress balance sheet, with over $350 billion in cash, or 30% of its current market value of $1.2 trillion.

So it isn't surprising that Berkshire has rallied as investors rotate out of technology and other artificial-intelligence plays into defensive groups like consumer stocks, real estate, and utilities.

Barron's has been bullish on Berkshire, but the stock doesn't look like a bargain now. The A shares traded Friday at $820,000 after overtaking the old high of about $810,000 set just before the May 2025 annual meeting. The B shares traded at $547. The stock is up 9% this year, still behind the S&P 500's 12% gain.

Berkshire trades for about 1.5 times our estimate of third-quarter book value — the company will probably report results on Nov. 7 — and 24 times projected 2026 operating earnings.

Those aren't excessive, but higher than the average of the past year. What about intrinsic value, Warren Buffett's favorite metric? The stock now trades above UBS analyst Brian Meredith's intrinsic value estimate of $815,000 per A share — one of the higher estimates on Wall Street.

A key issue for Berkshire is its cash deployment. Stock buybacks accelerated in July to over $3 billion, but shares were almost 10% lower then.

Are the buybacks continuing now, given a higher price? And will CEO Greg Abel find plays to invest in? One potential area is the AI space, where capital needs are massive. Berkshire invested $10 billion as part of Alphabet's $85 billion equity capital raise in June, boosting its stake to about $30 billion. Meta Platforms could come to market with a big equity deal by year end, and Berkshire could participate.

Endowment returns are finally beating the S&P 500, and Elon Musk is the reason. Harvard University recently said its endowment rose 27.1% in its fiscal year ending in June — outpacing the S&P's 22% total return. The endowment totaled $68 billion on June 30 — tops among U.S. universities.

SpaceX, which went public in June after a surge in its private-market value in the prior year, was a meaningful contributor to Harvard's strong performance.

Harvard is still trailing the S&P 500 over the past nine years — the tenure of the current endowment leadership — with an 11.4% annual return against 15% for the index.

This year could be tougher for Harvard and its alternatives-heavy portfolio, given the fallout in AI-related stocks. Big endowments have big weightings in private equity and venture capital, but Harvard's alternative allocation is extreme. It has just 14% in public stocks, some 5% in bonds and cash, 46% in private equity and venture capital, and 29% in hedge funds.

There is risk in the stock market, but there may be even greater danger in the Harvard model.

Write to Andrew Bary at andrew.bary@barrons.com

data.title: Bank of Canada to raise rates to 2.50% on October 28 and once again by end-March
data.description:
By Nushaiba Iqbal

The Bank of Canada will raise its overnight rate by 25 basis points to 2.50% on October 28 and follow with one more hike by the end of March to pre-empt any further rise in inflation expectations, according to a majority of economists polled by Reuters.

Inflation rose to 3.1% in September, only barely overshooting the BoC's target range of 1% to 3%. But the central bank's latest business outlook survey showed sharply rising inflation expectations in the run-up to a recent breakdown in trade talks with the United States, Canada's main export destination.

Quarterly inflation forecasts from the bank, also due next week, are likely to be revised higher, BoC Governor Tiff Macklem told reporters in remarks Saturday that markets interpreted as a hint a rate rise is coming.

Interest rate futures have moved from pricing in a 30% chance of a rate hike in October to around a three-in-four likelihood. Many economists this week changed their view from a hold to a hike, citing those remarks from Macklem.

"What changed the tone in the governor's public comments on the weekend and what changed our view on Monday is the same source, and that is the responses from the BoC's business outlook and consumer surveys," said Royce Mendes, managing director and head of macro strategy at Desjardins.

"So presumably the governor had seen the results before they were published more broadly on Monday. And I would assume that informed his public commentary," Mendes said. "The survey responses...suggest there are more serious inflationary pressures coming."

Nineteen of 34 economists surveyed in the October 21-23 poll, or 56% of them, said the BoC will hike its overnight rate by a quarter percentage point to 2.50%, its first move in a year.

This is a clear reversal from the previous poll, when 80% of respondents forecast the bank would hold its rate at 2.25% until the end of 2026, and two-thirds of them forecast a hold until the end of March 2027.

Those economists who forecast no move next week mainly cited a weak economy and subdued inflation pressures despite soaring oil prices , which hit $117 a barrel for the first time since May on Friday.

Sixteen of 29 respondents, a 55% majority, also forecast one more rise before March 2027, after which policymakers would hold the overnight rate at 2.75%, poll medians showed. If correct, it will be the shortest BoC policy tightening campaign in 30 years.

But even a short series of hikes would bring the BoC into a widening group of central banks that have opted for tighter monetary policy in response to persistent inflation emerging as a result of the US-led war with Iran that began in February.

Among major central banks, only the BoC and the Bank of England — which is widely expected to raise rates at its early November meeting — have not yet begun to raise rates.

But many say the BoC will need to be measured with the pace of rate increases given other risks to the economy.

Benjamin Reitzes, Canadian rates and macro strategist at BMO, said: "They'd rather make the mistake of hiking a little bit too early, which means maybe they have to hike a little bit less at the end of the day than falling behind the curve, which is what happened in 2021-2022, and they don't want to repeat that mistake.”

Economic growth likely slowed to 1.9% last quarter from 3.3% in Q2 and is forecast at 1.3% in the current one before accelerating next year, poll medians showed. The economy will grow 1.0% in 2026 and 1.7% in 2027, the survey found.

Inflation will average 2.8% for 2026 as a whole, falling to 2.3% in 2027, poll medians showed.

Winking Studios Limited (AIM / SGX:WKS) ("Winking Studios" or the "Company" and together with its subsidiaries, the "Group"), one of the leading global AAA game art outsourcing studios and an established game development company, announces that, further to the Mineloader Acquisition Announcement, and the announcement dated 21 October 2025 in relation to the issuance of new Incentive Shares in 2025, the Company will issue 1,573,176 new Incentive Shares in 2026 (the "2026 Incentive Shares") to the Key Management Personnel following the terms as set out in the Incentive Agreements.

Winking Studios completed the acquisition of Shanghai Mineloader Digital Technology Co., Ltd. ("Mineloader") on 1 April 2025. Specialising in higher margin AAA games from console platforms, Mineloader's service offerings in console platform games and established experience and presence in the global gaming industry is proving to be a valuable addition to the Group.

Prevailing General Share Issuance Mandate

As mentioned in the Mineloader Acquisition Announcement, the 2026 Incentive Shares are intended to be issued pursuant to the general share issuance mandate (the "General Mandate") obtained at the annual general meeting of the Company held on 30 April 2026 ("AGM").

Pursuant to the General Mandate, the maximum number of Shares that may be issued other than on a pro-rata basis for 2026 until the conclusion of the next annual general meeting of the Company or the date by which the next annual general meeting of the Company is required by law to be held, whichever is the earlier, is 220,969,059 Shares. Receipt of Listing and Quotation Notice from the Singapore Exchange Securities Trading Limited ("SGX-ST")

The Company has on 22 October 2026, received the in-principle approval for the listing of and quotation ("Notice") on the Catalist of the SGX-ST for the 2026 Incentive Shares, subject to compliance with the SGX-ST's listing requirements.

Please note that the Notice is not to be taken as an indication of the merits of the Company, its subsidiaries, its securities (including the 2026 Incentive Shares), or any related transaction contemplated by the Notice.

Admission and total voting rights

Application has been made to the London Stock Exchange for the admission of the 2026 Incentive Shares to trading on AIM.

The admission to trading of the 2026 Incentive Shares is expected to occur and dealings commence at 9.00 am (SGT) / 8.00 a.m. (GMT) on or around 28 October 2026 on the Catalist of the SGX-ST and AIM, respectively ("Admission"). On Admission, the 2026 Incentive Shares shall rank pari passu in all respects with the existing ordinary shares of the Company.

The number of ordinary shares in issue, and the total voting rights in the Company, on Admission, assuming no other changes to the Company's voting rights prior to Admission, will be 443,511,294, of which 2,479,200 ordinary shares are held in treasury, and, accordingly, the total number of voting rights is 441,032,094. data.title: Western Digital Gets Target Cut Despite Strong Earnings(EDIT1)
data.description:
TD Cowen cut its price target on Western Digital to $430 from $540, but kept a Buy rating after the storage company delivered a strong fiscal first quarter and issued an upbeat outlook.

Analyst Krish Sankar's revised target still implies roughly 21.4% upside from current levels.

The target cut was not driven by weaker demand.

Instead, Sankar lowered the valuation multiple he applies to Western Digital to 15 times earnings from 20 times, reflecting the company's plans to spend more aggressively on capacity expansion.

Western Digital reported $4.38 billion in fiscal Q1 2027 revenue, up 55.3% year over year and above the $4.14 billion consensus estimate.

Adjusted EPS came in at $4.64, beating Wall Street's $4.11 forecast.The company's guidance was even stronger. Western Digital expects $5.80 in EPS for fiscal Q2, roughly 20% above the $4.80 Wall Street had been expecting. Gross margin is projected at 60% to 61%. Sankar sees pricing as the biggest support for the bull case.

Average selling prices are expected to rise by a high-single-digit percentage next quarter and are already up 36% year over year. Most upcoming shipments are covered by long-term agreements, but that has not prevented Western Digital from raising prices.

Investor Takeaway

I think the most important part of TD Cowen's call is that the target cut is really about valuation discipline, not a weakening storage cycle.

Western Digital plans to increase capital spending from roughly $750 million in 2026 to $1.8 billion in 2027 and $2.3 billion in 2028 as it expands supply.

Even then, Sankar expects demand growth for nearline HDDs and enterprise SSDs of roughly 40% to 50% next year, potentially leaving industry supply short of demand.

That matters because HDDs remain dramatically cheaper than NAND storage on a per-terabyte basis.

TD Cowen estimates HDDs could remain 20 to 25 times cheaper per terabyte next year, giving cloud customers an economic incentive to keep buying even if prices rise.

For investors, the key things to watch are HDD pricing, exabyte growth, capex execution, hyperscaler demand and whether margins can stay near current elevated levels.

TD Cowen lowered the multiple.

It did not lower its conviction in the underlying storage cycle.

data.title: Bnode names Nicolas Baise CEO of Bpost unit, two executives to leave
data.description:
Belgian logistics group Bnode, formerly bpostgroup, on Friday named Chief Operations Officer Nicolas Baise as CEO of its Bpost business unit, effective January 1, 2027.

Baise replaces Chris Peeters, who has held the post on an interim basis since May 2025 alongside his group CEO role.

The company also said Chief Commercial Officer Christel Dendas and Chief Digital Officer Frank Croket will leave the company. Croket will remain during a transition period.
